subject: Query Regarding Time Difference Formatting in Camtrap R

messages.author: ef254f26d410a0ab
messages.subject: Query Regarding Time Difference Formatting in Camtrap R
parts:
Hello Camtrap R Community,

I have a question related to formatting time differences for using the timeshift function.

When working with time differences in the "years:months:days hours:minutes:seconds" format, I encountered a scenario where the difference is 40 days. I would like to clarify the appropriate way to express this duration in the specified format. Based on my understanding, I see two possible interpretations:

1. 00:00:40 00:00:00
This format indicates 40 days and zero hours, minutes, and seconds.
2. 00:01:10 00:00:00
This format implies a difference of 1 month, 10 days, and zero hours, minutes, and seconds.

Could you please provide some guidance on how to correctly format a time difference of 40 days in the "years:months:days hours:minutes:seconds" format? Additionally, if there are any other examples of larger time differences, I would greatly appreciate knowing those.

Best regards,
Orvill

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Query Regarding Time Difference Formatting in Camtrap R
parts:
Hello,
option 1 will be clearer and more well-defined. Option two can be anything from 28 and 41 days, depending on circumstances. For details please see the "Tricky" section in the help page of the time shift module of Exiftool. This is also mentioned in the function help.
Note that timeshift in exiftool is more flexible than in camtrapR - in camtrapR please stick to the "Y:M:D H:M:S" format.

If in doubt I'd recommend running the function with different sets of values on some test data and check the results. The "undo" parameter may be helpful here.
Best regards,
Jürgen
